name: anti-ai-design-style
description: Shared install contract. Every installer layer (install.sh, install.ps1) reads THIS and produces identical results. The GitHub owner is substituted at publish time.

runtime.note: Every scanner is plain Python with no third-party imports, so the hooks run on the python3 that ships with macOS and Linux. Playwright is optional and only adds the browser check; without it the proof line says 'rendered SKIPPED' and nothing fails.

hooks.why: Scans each UI file right after it is written and reports what reads as AI-made. Silent on every other file type.
Before the session ends, re-checks the UI files it touched so unscanned visual output is never presented as finished.

project_only.note: The five hookify warning rules load only from the folder you are working in. They cannot be installed globally. Run 'python3 <skill>/scripts/install.py .' inside a project to add them there.

surfaces.label: Codex
surfaces.no_hooks: Codex hook wiring could not be verified, so neither installer registers or claims it.
surfaces.note: Codex has no slash commands. The skill goes to the .agents/skills convention, which is also what this skill's own scripts/install.py --codex writes for a single project.

editors_are_manual.why: Adding the skill to Cursor, VS Code and the rest means running a third-party CLI (npx skills), which needs Node and downloads packages. Measured on 2026-09-12: it installs the skill to the shared ~/.agents/skills folder, not to anything editor-specific, while reporting a per-editor success. An installer that says 'cursor installed' when nothing cursor-shaped was written is lying, and installing Node and npm packages is not installing this skill. So both installers print the command and let the user run it knowingly.

installs_nothing_else.rule: Neither installer may install software other than this skill. No Node, no npm packages, no system package-manager calls, no third-party CLI.
installs_nothing_else.python: Needed only by the two hooks. If it is missing the installer says so, prints the one command to fix it, installs the files anyway and skips the hooks.

notes: The commands ship with a ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} placeholder. Outside a plugin that variable is unset, so every installer must replace it with the absolute path of the installed skill or the commands will call nothing.
A hook command containing a space breaks tool use in Claude Code. Every layer refuses to write a hook whose script path contains a space, and says so loudly rather than writing a broken one.
Uninstall removes only entries whose command contains 'anti-ai-design-style/scripts/', so hooks belonging to other tools are never touched.
